look_here_first: First decide whether the plant is woody: black dalea is a low intricately branched shrub with many tiny leaflets on pale gray/straw branchlets and short terminal flower spikes.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: many tiny obovate to oblanceolate leaflets on odd-pinnate leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: young twigs greenish to gray/straw and glandular

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: short terminal or leaf-opposed flower spikes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx nearly hairless outside but silky-ciliate around the mouth

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Low woody shrub/subshrub, usually under about 1 m.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually 4–9 pairs of tiny leaflets plus terminal leaflet; undersides gland-punctate.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Short terminal or leaf-opposed spikes, subcapitate to moderately dense.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: Short-toothed, glossy/glabrous externally, silky-ciliate around the mouth.

key_traits.label: Joey field observation
key_traits.text: Joey Santore's Pilostyles thurberi study documents Dalea frutescens as the host and includes exact wild Sutton County host-shrub, stem, leaf and parasite-emergence images. Use these as trusted private-study habit/ecology material.
